name: Machine Hip Thrust
grip: Hands steady the machine's handles; they do not lift the resistance.
description: A supported hip extension against a dedicated machine's resistance. Your upper back stays supported while your hips move the padded belt or lever.
setup: Follow the actual machine's instructions for the pad or belt, load and any safety catch.
Place your upper back on its support and feet firmly on the platform; adjust your position for the machine.
instructions: Brace the trunk and use the handles for stability.
Follow the machine's release sequence, then lower the hips under control.
Extend the hips until trunk and thighs are approximately aligned, without arching the lower back.
Return under control; re-engage the catch before releasing the belt or leaving.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher.
Changing foot position mid-set or releasing the restraint before securing the load.

logging.example: Two 20 kg plates: record 40 kg added load on this machine.
logging.note: Do not invent an empty-lever weight or compare loads across machines. A stack model needs a separate logging convention.

variantNote: Illustrated as a generic belt-loaded model. Selectorized and rigid-pad machines may use a different setup and release sequence.
